evals.name: named-lookup-turn-undead
evals.prompt: What does ACKS say about turning undead? I want to know how the cleric's class power works in 1e.
evals.expected_output: Cites rules/acore_core_classes.xml (cleric class power section) with line range. Returns a verbatim excerpt of the turn-undead mechanic. Uses the ACKS term 'turn undead' throughout (not 'rebuke undead'). Synthesizes how the d20-roll-vs-HD-indexed-target-value mechanic works.

evals.name: precedence-axioms-overrides-core
evals.prompt: How do thief skills work in ACKS? I'm implementing the proficiency throw mechanic for hear-noise, climb-walls, and the rest.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces BOTH the Axioms update (rules/ax_thief_skill_update.xml) AND the Core thief skill definitions (rules/acore_core_classes.xml). Treats the Axioms file as the canonical mechanic. Cites both with line ranges. Does not invent a unified-skill-check d20+modifier system from D&D.

evals.name: absent-rule-critical-hit
evals.prompt: How does ACKS handle critical hits? When I roll a natural 20 on my attack throw, what happens?
evals.expected_output: States clearly that ACKS 1e does not have a generic critical-hit rule. References cleaving (rules/acore_combat_and_wounds.xml) as the closest analogue with a citation. Does NOT invent a critical-hit system from D&D/Pathfinder. Asks Jedidiah whether a designed critical-hit system in generation/ is wanted, or whether attack throws should stay flat.

evals.name: bleed-through-rebuke-undead
evals.prompt: Write a short GDD section describing how clerics rebuke undead, including the dice mechanic and how it scales with cleric level.
evals.expected_output: Catches the bleed-through term 'rebuke undead' and substitutes 'turn undead'. Either (a) explicitly notes that ACKS uses 'turn undead' and proceeds with the ACKS mechanic, citing rules/acore_core_classes.xml, or (b) asks for confirmation that the user meant 'turn undead' before drafting. Does NOT draft a D&D-flavored rebuke-undead mechanic.

evals.name: structural-lookup-condition
evals.prompt: What are the mechanical effects of the blinded condition in ACKS? I need to wire it into the combat system.
evals.expected_output: Cites rules/ax_conditions_catalog.xml (the <condition name='blinded'> block) with line range. Returns the verbatim effects: -2 to surprise rolls, -4 to attack throws, movement reduced to 1/4. Does NOT add D&D-style effects like 'attacks against the creature have advantage' or 'creature attacks have disadvantage' that aren't in the ACKS block.

evals.name: free-text-mortal-wounds
evals.prompt: I need to implement mortal wounds resolution. Find me the relevant rules and procedures.
evals.expected_output: Returns the Axioms mortal wounds file (rules/ax_mortal_wounds_and_tampering.xml) and the combat-and-wounds file (rules/acore_combat_and_wounds.xml) where mortal wounds is referenced. Cites both with line ranges. Notes the missing tables that the Core extraction flagged (per the <coverage> block in the XML). Does NOT invent the mortal wounds table results from memory.

evals.name: ambiguous-territory-classification
evals.prompt: I'm working on the wilderness generation system. Tell me about the Outlands territory classification.
evals.expected_output: Catches the bleed-through term 'Outlands'. States that ACKS 1e has three territory classifications: Civilized, Borderlands, Wilderness. Cites the rules file where these are defined (likely acore_axioms_strongholds_and_domains.xml or similar). Does NOT invent an 'Outlands' classification. Asks the user whether they meant Wilderness, Borderlands, or something else.

evals.name: code-comment-citation
evals.prompt: I'm writing the initiative roll function in GDScript. Give me the function with a proper citation comment for the ACKS 1e initiative rule.
evals.expected_output: Looks up initiative in rules/acore_combat_and_wounds.xml (around line 55-77). Produces a GDScript function with a `# RAW: rules/acore_combat_and_wounds.xml:NNN-MMM — ...` comment that glosses the rule (1d6 + Dex, high acts first, ties simultaneous, long-reach/readied missile interrupts). Uses 1d6 not 1d20 for initiative. The comment is self-documenting.
